scenario_prompt: Write a two-paragraph executive summary addressed directly to a fictional buyer's Chief Financial Officer, recommending a cloud migration. Context: a mid-market freight brokerage firm is moving its load-matching and carrier-settlement systems off on-premises Microsoft SQL Server (28 instances) running on Hyper-V (620 virtual machines) onto Google Cloud, targeting Google Compute Engine for compute and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL for the data layer, over a 2-year, $4,200,000 programme. The CFO has stated she is measured on reducing the current $1,850,000 annual technology spend and on a clean DOT compliance audit, which opens in 6 months. Cover why this matters to her now and what she should expect from the programme. Return only the summary text, two paragraphs, no headers.
text:
**Executive summary**

No RFP text, discovery notes, or other customer source material was supplied beyond the scenario stated in this prompt; the provenance override in PF-3.3 cannot fire, so every term below is judged by the deletion test alone rather than retained as the buyer's own wording.

You are running 28 on-premises Microsoft SQL Server instances across 620 Hyper-V virtual machines to support load-matching and carrier-settlement, at an annual technology spend of $1,850,000 [PF-1.14: figure and baseline as stated in the scenario provided to this task]. You are measured on reducing that spend and on a clean DOT compliance audit opening in six months, and both pressures compound now: every month this estate stays on-premises is a month closer to that audit window with settlement data still tied to hardware you maintain directly. We propose a two-year, $4,200,000 migration of load-matching and carrier-settlement off this Hyper-V estate onto Google Cloud — replacing fixed VM and SQL Server licensing costs with Compute Engine for the workloads that need to scale with load volume, and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL for a managed data layer that isolates and logs the settlement data your auditors will review [PF-1.9: capability named before product]. [PF-2.17 REVIEW (compliance): this document does not verify Google Cloud's specific certifications against DOT audit requirements — that mapping needs confirming before the audit date is cited as a driver]. [PF-2.11 GAP: neither a percentage reduction in the $1,850,000 baseline nor a comparable customer benchmark for this migration size was supplied — do not state a savings figure until one is measured or a reference is provided].

For you, success looks like two things landing before the audit opens and beyond it: a technology cost base that moves from the current $1,850,000 run-rate toward a lower, cloud-consumption-based figure your finance team can track monthly instead of at renewal, and a settlement data platform your auditors can inspect without your team defending 28 separate SQL Server configurations. [PF-2.14 REVIEW (commitment): "the programme will reduce spend" and any date-bound audit-readiness promise need confirming as intended contractual commitments, not aspirational framing, before this ships]. [PF-2.4 GAP: no named differentiator over an alternative migration approach or vendor was supplied — this summary does not claim Google Cloud is uniquely capable until a specific, evidenced comparable is provided]. What you should expect over the two years is a phased cutover from the 620-VM Hyper-V estate rather than a single switchover, with cost and audit-readiness milestones reported against the $1,850,000 baseline at each phase; the specific milestone dates and interim cost checkpoints are not yet defined and are marked below rather than estimated.

## Unresolved before this document is sent

| Marker | Rule | What is needed |
|---|---|---|
| Compliance certification mapping to DOT audit requirements | PF-2.17 | Confirmation of which Google Cloud certifications/controls map to the specific DOT audit criteria in scope |
| Savings percentage / comparable migration benchmark | PF-2.11 | A measured savings target or a named comparable of similar scale to cite instead of an invented figure |
| "Programme will reduce spend" / audit-readiness promise | PF-2.14 | Confirmation these are intended as contractual commitments before they ship in buyer-facing language |
| Differentiator over alternative approach or vendor | PF-2.4 | A specific, evidenced capability this vendor can deliver that an alternative cannot, or removal of any implied uniqueness |
| Phase milestone dates and interim cost checkpoints | PF-2.13 | Defined phase dates and interim cost/audit checkpoints for the 2-year programme |
